It gives up Poland, the Baltic provinces, Finland, Ukraine — territory holding a large part of the Empire's population, coal and grain. It is signed because there is no army left with which to decline it. The front that could not be held in 1915 without shells could not be held in 1918 without men, and the men walked home.Settled recordEast Prussia: entered early, on the undertaking to France. 1915: the salient was given up and the army kept. August 1915: the Emperor assumed the supreme command in person. 1916: the South-Western Front attacked alone and spent its best divisions doing it. March 1917: the front commanders declined to advise. June 1917: the offensive was made. Autumn 1914: Galicia was reinforced. The Emperor at headquarters: the capital did not hold together in his absence. The Second Army, August 1914: left to press on. The Carpathians, March 1915: pressed on into the mountains. The Guards, summer 1916: kept in reserve. Romania: three divisions sent. The death penalty: restored at the front on 12 July 1917. The Kornilov affair: the dismissal refused, and the march collapsed.
